The term largely corresponds to 'garden plant', though the latter is much less precise, as any plant may be grown in a garden. Ornamental plants are plants that are grown for display purposes, rather than functional ones. While some plants are both ornamental and functional, people usually use the term  ornamental plants  to refer to plants which have no value beyond being attractive, although many people feel that this is value enough. Ornamental plants are the keystone of ornamental gardening, and they come in a range of shapes, sizes, and colors suitable to a broad array of climates, landscapes, and gardening needs. Some ornamental plants are foliage plants grown mainly or entirely for their showy foliage; this is especially true of houseplants. Their foliage may be deciduous, turning bright orange, red, and yellow before dropping off in the fall, or evergreen, in which case it stays green year-round. Some ornamental foliage has a striking appearance created by lacy leaves or long needles, while other ornamentals are grown for distinctively colored leaves, such as silvery-gray ground covers and bright red grasses, among many others. During the entire time I was browsing the menu the waitress continued to be a one man show, seating other customers and delivering food and drink all by self, all the while making small talk with her guest, providing exceptional customer service. The food was out pretty fast and in a fairly large portion size too, it wasn't too spicy and was extremely tasty, now that I know this place is nearby I'm going to come back again in the future to try their other menu items. This location does a lot of take out so there's never a wait to sit and the service is quick. Wow, so good! Still thinking about our meal here and it's been almost 2 weeks. It was not full and we were a large party of 6. Service was great and the ladies were kind and prompt. My favorites were the Singapore noodles and the donburi bowl with beef. The shrimp with spicy mayo was also delish! We shared the different plates and everyone left satisfied. 107 Taste in coral gables is a great addition to the area, I've been to the Miami Lakes location many times but the size of Coral Gables and how yummy rb food was makes me want to come back for more! I'm on a quest for good broth with a depth of flavor and noodles right now! I actually enjoyed the food at the FIU location but shared my disappointment regarding the overall cleanliness of that locationthe Coral Gables location was the exact opposite. Clean from the door to the table. I did not visit the lavatory but I plan to return and check those important details soon! I remain a fan of the food. Decided to order the exact same - Hell's Ramen and chicken karaage. Actually a tad spicier than the FIU meal. I'm a fan of spice so that works for me. My date enjoyed his udon bowl and bao buns. We both enjoyed a pot of hot green tea! One young man in the front of house. He worked up to 4 tables and provided take out services to customers. He was overwhelmed from time to time but he managed. It may be helpful to have a little assistance when restaurant is busy. I would have ordered dessert but it felt like I was adding to the burdens of the lone waiter. Definitely will return to this location in the near future.

In 1953, a Jacksonville, Florida, man named Keith Kramer, along with his wife's uncle Matthew Burns, looked to create a restaurant idea of their own after being inspired by the original McDonald's restaurant in San Bernardino, California. As part of their new restaurant, they bought the rights to a special grill machine called the Insta-Broiler, and named their restaurant "Insta-Burger King. " Several years later, the idea had grown into several restaurant locations and was picked up by a pair of Cornell University classmates, James McLamore and David Edgerton. CIaim Your UPS Rewards Here Before Sept 3rd http://www.asgcip.net/transpired-stormy/bac4h2395e8s6T10j190eh713l21uFv4GIf4rxvs4FhIHEsvZ7qQgnRd97c1zJ0JW5XJiLb Airmail, the rapid system of delivering mail by aircraft, has significantly transformed communication over the past century. The birth of airmail can be traced back to the early 20th century when aviation pioneers started experimenting with mail transportation via air. One of the most crucial benefits of airmail is its ability to significantly reduce the delivery time of messages, documents, and packages. Its astonishing to look back and see how far we've come from the days of the Pony Express to airmail. The initiative of transporting mail by air was initially risky, and many doubted its success. However, brave aviators took on the challenge, sometimes facing treacherous weather conditions, to ensure that mail reached its destination. Over the years, advancements in aircraft technology, combined with effective organizational systems, have made airmail a staple in mail delivery systems worldwide. The introduction of jet engines shortened delivery times even further, allowing for international correspondence to be as swift as domestic. Apart from speed, airmail also allowed for the expansion of commerce and communication into remote areas of the world. Some regions, inaccessible by land or sea due to geographical barriers, became reachable thanks to the flexibility of air transport. Stamps play a unique role in the story of airmail. Specialized airmail stamps, often at a higher price point than regular stamps, became collectors' items and a testament to the prestige of air mail. These stamps often bore illustrations of aircraft, emphasizing the novelty and excitement of this new form of mail delivery. As with any service, there were challenges along the way. Weather, especially in the early days, posed a considerable threat. Navigation was another challenge, as pilots had to rely heavily on landmarks during daylight and large bonfires at night to guide their paths. By the mid-20th century, improvements in radar technology and air traffic control systems mitigated many of these challenges. This, combined with larger cargo capacities and faster aircraft, further solidified the role of airmail in global communication. In todays digital age, where emails and instant messages are the norm, one might wonder about the relevance of airmail. However, the shipment of goods, documents, and other tangible items via air remains an indispensable part of our globalized world. E-commerce, for instance, relies heavily on air transport to meet the delivery expectations of customers worldwide. The legacy of airmail is not just in its contribution to fast communication but also in how it paved the way for the global aviation industry. On March 29, 1971, Air Southwest Co. changed its name to Southwest Airlines Co. with headquarters in Dallas. Southwest began scheduled passenger service on June 18, 1971, on two routes: between Dallas Love Field and Houston Intercontinental Airport and between Dallas Love Field and San Antonio with three Boeing 737-200s. Service between Houston Hobby Airport and Dallas Love Field and between Houston Hobby and San Antonio began on November 14, 1971.
